title: LLM4Vuln: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Decoupling and Enhancing LLMs' Vulnerability Reasoning

key_numbers.metric: knowledge-enhancement effect on F1 (Solidity, foundation models)
key_numbers.value: F1 nearly doubling on average with knowledge vs. without

key_numbers.metric: context-supplementation effect on TP counts across 36 knowledge x prompt combinations
key_numbers.value: Solidity 22/36 increased, Java 18/36 increased, C/C++ 28/36 increased
14 confirmed vulnerabilities of 29 submitted, $3,576 in bounties across 4 projects

structure_gain: Context supplementation (caller/related-function context) increased TP in 22/36 (Solidity), 18/36 (Java), 28/36 (C/C++) knowledge x prompt combinations vs. the no-context condition, same model/budget (RQ2).
stop_detail: Caller/related-function context is statically extracted and serialized directly into the prompt; knowledge grounding uses either the LLM's own knowledge, raw retrieved vulnerability reports (FAISS top-3), or GPT-4.1-summarized knowledge, per the knowledge/context prompt templates (Fig. 4, Sec. III-IV).

title: Vul-RAG: Enhancing LLM-based Vulnerability Detection via Knowledge-level RAG

key_numbers.metric: Pair accuracy gain vs code-level RAG baseline
key_numbers.where: Main results / comparison to code-level RAG

key_numbers.metric: Manual detection accuracy with generated explanations

structure_gain: Knowledge-level RAG (structured multi-dimensional vulnerability knowledge) beats code-level RAG (raw code retrieval) by 16-27 points pair accuracy; beats a fine-tuning baseline (LLMAO) by 22-26 points
stop_detail: Iteratively checks each retrieved knowledge item's vulnerability cause against the presence/absence of its fix before flagging code as vulnerable (knowledge-level RAG detection procedure)

title: CGP-Tuning: Structure-Aware Soft Prompt Tuning for Code Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: Removing the graph-to-text cross-modal alignment module (which fuses the CPG-derived GAT embeddings into soft prompts) drops accuracy by 14.5-18.75pp across three frozen LLM backbones, same soft-prompt tuning budget otherwise
stop_detail: No natural-language grounding output: graph structure enters the LLM only as opaque continuous soft-prompt embeddings, not a readable/verifiable text trace (soft prompt tuning section)

title: LLM-BSCVM: An LLM-Based Blockchain Smart Contract Vulnerability Management Framework
structure_gain: Removing RAG (retrieved audit reports / similar-contract corpus) drops F1 from 0.9104 to 0.8440 (-6.64pp); a full-context variant LLM-BSCVM(E) that injects more retrieved text actually underperforms (80.42% accuracy) due to noise
stop_detail: Patch Verification Agent runs a multi-agent debate among independent models to confirm a repair eliminates the vulnerability without introducing new ones before finalizing (Verifier agent description)

title: Tracing Errors, Constructing Fixes: Repository-Level Memory Error Repair via Typestate-Guided Context Retrieval

key_numbers.metric: correct patches, full LTFix vs. LTFix-NT (no context trace) ablation
total errors fixed, full LTFix vs. LTFix-F (file-level context) ablation
repair success rate (custom benchmark / SAVER dataset)

structure_gain: Full LTFix (typestate-guided context trace) vs. LTFix-NT (error-propagation path only, no context trace), same LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet): 22 vs. 15 correct patches (+47%), 37 vs. 22 total errors fixed (+68%), 1 vs. 4 new errors introduced (Section 5.7 ablation, RQ3).
stop_detail: A finite typestate automaton instruments dynamic execution (via GDB) to record memory-object state transitions only at typestate-changing statements, producing an error-propagation path (nearest allocation to error point) and a context trace that are serialized into the LLM prompt (Algorithm 1, methodology section).

title: ZeroFalse: Improving Precision in Static Analysis with LLMs

key_numbers.metric: F1 gain, optimized vs minimal-context prompt (OpenVuln)

structure_gain: Optimized vs minimal-context prompt: average F1 +0.176 across 10 models (OpenVuln, Table 4), same models.
stop_detail: One-shot, schema-constrained JSON adjudication per alert with no iterative agent loop or fine-tuning; every prompt/response pair is logged for audit (LLM adjudication section)

title: CKG-LLM: LLM-Assisted Detection of Smart Contract Access Control Vulnerabilities Based on Knowledge Graphs

key_numbers.metric: avg detection time per contract vs baselines

structure_gain: none reported for representation directly (the knowledge-graph structure is held constant); reported gains are from fine-tuning stages: F1 rises Base 57.8% -> SFT 65.5% -> SFT+DPO 74.9% (Table 1), not a raw-text-vs-KG ablation.
stop_detail: Slither's IR is traversed to build a two-layer (ontology+instance) contract knowledge graph capturing control-flow, invocation, and inheritance relations (Sec 3.1); the SFT+DPO-tuned LLM translates NL vulnerability patterns into SPARQL queries executed against this graph to ground detections (Sec 3.2).

title: MulVul: Retrieval-augmented Multi-Agent Code Vulnerability Detection via Cross-Model Prompt Evolution

key_numbers.value: MulVul 34.79% vs GPT-4o 3.86% vs LLM x CPG 24.58% vs LLMVulExp 22.72% vs VISION 18.12%

structure_gain: Removing retrieval: Macro-F1 34.56% -> 21.80% (-12.76pp), same model (the -30.70 figure belongs to the GPT-4o baseline row).
stop_detail: Router and Detector agents call retrieval tools to pull evidence from vulnerability knowledge bases (CWE/pattern databases) during multi-agent coarse-to-fine classification, grounding predictions to reduce hallucination (retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework section, Table 4 ablation).

structure_gain: none reported (no RAG-vs-no-RAG ablation; single-system LLM-judge quality scores only, no unstructured/raw-text baseline comparator)
stop_detail: A RAG engine embeds and retrieves from 70 Google Project Zero root-cause-analysis reports and 1,321 MITRE CWE entries using vector similarity, BM25-hybrid, or HyPE (hypothetical-question) retrieval, feeding passages to the Analyst/Reporter agents that draft the vulnerability report.

title: VulTriage: Triple-Path Context Augmentation for LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: Removing the structural Control Path (AST/CFG/DFG-derived) drops P-C from 55 to 42 (-23.6% relative) and raises errors from 76 to 89, same GPT-4o backend and test subset (Table 2).
stop_detail: The Semantic Path is prompt-constrained to describe only directly observable code behaviors, avoiding speculation about programmer intent -- a soft prompting constraint, not a formal or external verification mechanism.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: CWE-415 F1 gain (Claude Code, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 F1 gain (Codex, LeanGuard vs Pure LLM)
CWE-416 / CWE-415 F1 vs Pure LLM (same DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

structure_gain: LeanGuard (AST-extraction + Lean 4 verification) vs Pure LLM, identical DeepSeek-V4-Pro backend and temperature=0: F1 +0.135 (CWE-416) and +0.191 (CWE-415) (Table IV) -- a clean same-model comparison isolating the neurosymbolic pipeline's contribution.
stop_detail: The evidence-aware adjudicator (Section IV-G, Table III) grades symbolic (Q_Lean: strong/weak/noisy/none) and neural (Q_LLM: strong/weak/none) verdicts by evidence quality and lets a high-evidence verdict override a low-evidence one (e.g., Lean 'strong' VULNERABLE overrides neural 'none' SAFE) -- this is the paper's core grounding mechanism against premature discharge of safety obligations.
